page.layout: One printed page of running text in one column; in the right margin two notes, beside the first and second paragraphs of the text. The running head is at the top left, the page number at the top right.

main_text.p: Carolus V. omnium Imperatorum potentissimus fuit.
Quippe qui cum Imperio amplissima Hispaniæ regna & ditiones Austriacas conjunxit,
Pax Monasterienfis Imperii statum vehementer mutavit.7. Sta-tum ho-diernū

Quippe inter cætera contra Au-ream Bullam octavus Electoratus constitutus fuit, titulo Archi Thesaurarii: Galliæ quoq; & Sveciæ Reges, ille Alsatiam, hic Pomeraniam, Episcopatum Bremensem & Verdensem adepti sunt.

page.notes: Right margin, first note: "6. Statū sub Ca-rolo V.", beside the paragraph "Carolus V." (placed above as a note; in the text it stands beside "Canon 10." and "Carolus V."). Second note, "7. Sta-tum ho-diernū", stands beside the paragraph "Pax Monasterienfis". The first note was not placed in the paragraph text above, because I could not place it with certainty; it belongs with the Carolus V. paragraph. Doubtful: the page number "53" at the top right is printed in old-style figures and could be read differently. The small ornament after "fuit", "mutavit" and "sunt" is a printer's mark, not transcribed. The sign after "Explic." and the pointed mark at the foot are not transcribed. The left edge shows the neighbouring page and is left out.
